correctness.rationale: For n≥2 and Ω(n),Ω(n+1)≤2, the even member is either 2, 4, or 2p with p odd prime. Direct λ values of (2,3),(3,4),(4,5) leave only (3,4). For even e=2p, λ(e)=p−1; odd adjacent o=2p±1 is prime, an odd square r², or qr with odd primes q<r. A prime o has λ(o)=o−1>p−1. For square o=2p−1, λ(o)=r(r−1)>(r²−1)/2=p−1; for o=2p+1, equality reduces to r²−2r+3=0 with negative discriminant. For distinct qr set d=gcd(q−1,r−1)≥2≤q−1. Equating λ(qr)=(q−1)(r−1)/d with p−1 yields (2−d)qr=2q+2r−2−d (o=2p−1) or (2−d)qr=2q+2r−2−3d (o=2p+1). Left side ≤0 but both RHS >0, using d≤q−1. Exhausts all cases. Independent separate exact Carmichael factorization enumerated n=2..9999 with only n=3 under Ω bounds, corroborating but not proving the infinite case.
